key_insight: Light Coils replace nearly all galvanic MRI receiver cabling with optical links for data, power, and detuning, enabling scalable receive arrays with conventional SNR performance.
engineering_relevance: This architecture could simplify high-density MRI coil arrays by reducing cabling complexity, electromagnetic coupling, and safety constraints while preserving clinical image quality.
method: Use Mach-Zehnder modulators to imprint each coil's MR signal onto a C-band optical carrier.
Deliver front-end power via power-over-fiber and photovoltaic conversion.
Control active detuning through a pulse-sequence-triggered optical path; extend to multi-channel readout with dense wavelength-division multiplexing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports single-channel in vivo 3T brain imaging comparable to coaxial readout, plus a four-channel fiber-multiplexed demo with >28 dB inter-channel optical isolation and reduced noise correlation.
watch_item: Practical deployment still depends on precise joint tuning of modulator bias, optical power, and front-end gain, which may complicate system integration and robustness.
paper_title: Light Coils: MRI with Fully Optical Data and Power Transmission
